# Learning log

Dated list of concepts introduced by pull requests, newest first. Add one file per PR that teaches something new (a pattern, a tool, a technique) at `docs/handbook/learning-log/<issue>-<slug>.md`, then run `pnpm learning-log:index`.

| 2026-10-25 | #247 | The options panel is a controlled component: the page owns the value, the panel only shows it and reports edits. Its numbers come from the engine (ease table) and from `@tafsila/schemas` (limits, `buildEngineOptions`), so the browser preview and the API save build identical options. Ease constants come through a constants-only engine entry so no geometry reaches the main bundle. | [React](tech/react.md) |
| 2026-10-25 | #246 | The picker shows every feature through one table that lists the fields of each section and one generic panel, so adding a feature means adding a row, and a test fails until it is added; length overrides take centimetres in the box and millimetres in the design, and their limits are an engine export so the screen never owns a number | [Zustand](tech/zustand.md) |
| 2026-10-25 | #244 | The design picker keeps the spec being edited in a small Zustand store whose steps are plain functions, so undo, dirty checks and the browser draft are tested without React; the sections shown come from the engine's `specOptions`, and the engine rules are imported by a subpath so the geometry stays out of page bundles | [Zustand](tech/zustand.md) |
| 2026-10-25 | #243 | The viewer draws a `PatternScene` the engine builds in the worker, so the page never does geometry. Zoom and pan are pure functions (easy to test); gestures use Pointer Events so mouse, touch and pen share one path, and a pinch is just two pointers. The canvas never mirrors in Arabic; only the buttons do. | [PatternScene](glossary.md#pattern-scene) |

| 2026-10-24 | #241 | The 60 picker drawings are lists of SVG path strings drawn by one component with `currentColor`, keyed by the schema enums, so a new option without a drawing fails the type check and a test. | [Design system and RTL](../frontend/README.md) |
| 2026-10-24 | #240 | A group of picture cards is a radio group (arrows) for one choice and a set of checkboxes (Tab, Space) for several; a disabled card shows its reason as visible text so touch and screen-reader users see it too, and the drawing is a slot the feature fills | [Storybook](tech/storybook.md) |
| 2026-10-19 | #245 | The browser never sends a finished pattern. | 2026-10-19 | #242 | The designs list shows how many versions each design has, its status and the client's name. | 2026-10-19 | #239 | The browser drafts the pattern in a Web Worker so typing never freezes the page: a small client keeps only the latest request, a controller debounces by 250 ms, and a build-output scan fails CI if the engine geometry ever leaks into a page bundle. | 2026-10-19 | #238 | The engine now exposes what a design may contain: `specRefusals` is the single list of refused combinations (the same predicates the modules use), `specOptions` marks each value allowed or refused with an Arabic and English reason, `defaultSpec` gives a valid start per category and `normalizeSpec` repairs any design by changing the add-on that clashes. Tests and the future picker read the same list, so they can never disagree. | [Engine README, picker rules](../engine/README.md#picker-rules) |
| 2026-10-19 | #237 | A version table that users can only read and add to (no update or delete grant) keeps history honest, and a composite foreign key on (design_id, owner_id) lets the database itself refuse a version that points at someone else's design. | 2026-10-19 | #147 | A property test draws random designs (filtered by the engine's own compatibility rules) and random bodies from the 25-body matrix, and checks that every result is valid. Bugs found by a test are reported, not fixed in the same PR. | [Property testing](tech/fast-check.md) |
| 2026-10-19 | #146 | The sewing order is not written per module. | 2026-10-19 | #145 | Pockets, belt and lining are late engine modules that only add or copy pieces: a pocket is a notch on the side seam plus a bag, the belt is a strip split at the fabric width, and the lining is a copy of the shell with its hem lifted. | 2026-10-19 | #144 | Which parts a dress, a skirt or a blouse needs is a small table, so a spec the AI fills with a missing part becomes a bilingual refusal instead of a crash, and an extra part is a warning. A one-piece dress keeps the bodice above the waist and the skirt below the hip and redraws only the zone between, so the waist dart becomes a fisheye and the princess seam runs on to the hem. | [Fisheye dart](glossary.md#fisheye-dart) · [Feature module](glossary.md#feature-module) · [decision 144](../decisions/144-garment-assembly.md) |
| 2026-10-19 | #143 | Every garment module draws its pieces on the fold first; the closure module runs last and changes only what the opening needs. It finds the pieces along the opening by their stable ids and edge names, top to bottom, so a zip-stop notch can land on the skirt even though the length is counted from the neck. A zip turns a fold into a seam and widens its allowance; buttons move the centre line out by the extension and mark the buttons on the old centre line. The extension is an overlap, not body, so the body lines declare it and the circumference check leaves it out instead of failing. | [Closure](glossary.md#closure) · [Button extension](glossary.md#button-extension) · [Facing](glossary.md#facing) · [decision 143](../decisions/143-closures.md) |
| 2026-10-19 | #142 | Every sleeve style starts from the set-in block, so the cap height, the ease and the balance notches stay as the block sets them. A cap sleeve or flutter covers only part of the armhole, so it declares the armhole it is not sewn to. | 2026-10-19 | #141 | Each collar reads the neck the bodice already has and never redraws it. The peter pan traces the front and back necks with a rigid move (mirror, lay on the shoulder, turn for the roll), and a rigid move keeps every length, so its neck edge is the bodice neck. A stand gets its CF curve first and makes the straight part from CB whatever length is left, so it is as long as the half neck without any search. Splitting the collar neck at the shoulder lets each half pair with the bodice piece it sews to, and the notches the collar declares are copied onto the bodice by the finishing step. Combinations the method cannot draft (a collar on a V neck, a closed stand) are refused with a message instead of drawn wrong. | [Collar](glossary.md#collar) · [Stand](glossary.md#stand) · [Turn of cloth](glossary.md#turn-of-cloth) · [decision 141](../decisions/141-collars.md) |
| 2026-10-19 | #140 | A contour band or waist facing is traced from the skirt's own waist: each part past a dart is turned about the dart's tip until the two legs meet. A one-piece band instead splits its sewn edge into one run per cut copy of each skirt piece, so every run pairs with the skirt edge it sews to; anything that is longer on purpose (the closure underlap, gathers, pleats) is declared, never hidden. The round family adapts its handles to the depth/width ratio, the V turns one way only, and the sweetheart is built from circular arcs whose radii leave room for the facing; depths that would force a tighter bend are clamped with a warning instead of drawn. | [Neckline](glossary.md#neckline) · [Facing and interfacing](glossary.md#facing) · [decision 139](../decisions/139-necklines-facings.md) |
